# Basic Guidelines for Pump Performance

NPSHA CALCULATIONS

1) CASE No. 3 : PUMP DRAWING WATER FROM A CLOSED VESSEL UNDER VACUUM

DATA :

1) VACUUM IN VESSEL = 600 mm of mercury
2) LIQUID TEMPERATURE = $40^\circ\text{ C}$
3) LIQUID LEVEL ABOVE PUMP CENTRE = 10.2 meters
4) FRICTION LOSSES IN SUCTION PIPE ILINE SYSTEM = 1 meter
5) VAPOUR PRESSURE = $0.49\text{ kg}/\text{cm}^2$
6) SP. GRAVITY OF LIQUID = 0.72

METHOD :

$\text{ha} = \frac{10 \times 1}{0.72} = 13.89\text{ meters of liquid}$

$\text{hvp} = \frac{10 \times 0.49}{0.72} = 6.81\text{ meters of liquid}$

$\text{Ps} = 600\text{ mm of Hg}$
$= \frac{600}{1000} \times \frac{13.6}{0.72} = 11.33\text{ meters of liquid}$

($\because$ 13.6 is specific gravity of mercury )

$\text{hs} = \text{hsl} - \text{Ps} - \text{hfs}$
$= 10.2 - 11.33 - 1$
$= -2.13\text{ meters of liquid ( suction lift exists )}$

$\text{NPSHA} = \text{ha} \pm \text{hs} - \text{hvp} = 13.89 - 2.13 - 6.81 = 4.95\text{ meters}$

[Diagram labels: 600 mm OF Hg VACUUM, 10.2 M.]

NPSHA CALCULATIONS

1) CASE No. 4 : PUMP DRAWING LIQUID UNDER PRESSURE FROM A CLOSED TANK.

DATA :

1) PRESSURE IN CLOSED VESSEL = $0.5\text{ kg}/\text{cm}^2$
2) ATMOSPHERIC PRESSURE AT INSTALLATION = $0.9\text{ kg}/\text{cm}^2$
3) LIQUID LEVEL IN A VESSEL ABOVE THE PUMP CENTRE LINE = 0.2 meters
4) FRICTION LOSSES IN SUCTION PIPE LINE SYSTEM = 1.5 meters
5) VAPOUR PRESSURE OF LIQUID = $0.45\text{ kg}/\text{cm}^2$
6) SP. GRAVITY OF LIQUID = 0.8

METHOD :

$\text{ha} = \frac{10 \times 0.9}{0.8} = 11.25\text{ meters of liquid}$

$\text{hvp} = \frac{10 \times 0.45}{0.8} = 5.625\text{ meters of liquid}$

$\text{Ps} = \frac{10 \times 0.5}{0.8} = 6.25\text{ meters of liquid}$

NOW

$\text{hs} = \text{hsl} + \text{Ps} - \text{hfs}$
$= 0.2 + 6.25 - 1.5$
$= 4.95\text{ meters of liquid ( suction head exists )}$

$\text{NPSHA} = \text{ha} \pm \text{hs} - \text{hvp}$
$= 11.25 + 4.95 - 5.625$
$= 10.575\text{ meters}$

[Diagram labels: $0.5\text{ kg}/\text{cm}^2$ PRESSURE, 0.2 M.]
